Page.signature: Page(blocks: (Heading | Text | CodeBlock | CodeDiff | CodeWalkthrough | Callout | Steps | Table | DescriptionList | Accordion | Cards | Logos | TerminalReplay | AgentReplay | Chat | Figure | Diagram | Artifact)[])
Page.description: The whole page: its blocks, top to bottom, in one column. Always the root.

Heading.description: A section heading. The page title is shown already, so level 2 for sections and 3 for subsections. Prefer role headings that say what kind of section it is.

Text.description: Running text in Markdown: paragraphs, short lists (up to 5 points), **bold**, `inline code` and links. No headings, no code fences and no tables here.

CodeBlock.signature: CodeBlock(code: string, language?: string, title?: string)
CodeBlock.description: Code that simply is: a file, a command, a folder tree. Name it by its file (title) when it is one. Paste the real code; never describe code in prose. Long code that is only read goes here too, not in a CodeWalkthrough.

CodeDiff.signature: CodeDiff(before: string, after: string, file?: string)
CodeDiff.description: A change to a file: the code before and after, played as an edit. Use it instead of two CodeBlocks when the point is what changed.

CodeWalkthrough.description: Code built or read step by step: the reader scrolls the steps while the code stays beside them and each step lights up its lines. For a file that grows (a route, then a second one) or a short piece explained line by line. 2 to 5 steps.

WalkthroughStep.signature: WalkthroughStep(title: string, text: string, code: string, highlight?: string)
WalkthroughStep.description: One step of a CodeWalkthrough: a short title, what it explains in Markdown, the whole code as it stands at this step (not only what changes), and the line numbers it is about ("4-7"), left out to light up the lines it adds.

Callout.description: An aside set apart from the text: note, tip, important, warning or caution, one kind per thing. Its text is Markdown. Never two in a row, and never for the main idea.

Steps.description: Numbered steps for a procedure the reader follows in order (install, configure, run). For code that grows step by step, use CodeWalkthrough; for commands and their output, TerminalReplay.

StepItem.description: One step: a short title and its explanation in Markdown.

Table.signature: Table(columns: string[], rows: string[][], caption?: string)
Table.description: A comparison or structured facts: column headers and rows of short cells (Markdown inline: `code`, **bold**). Use it whenever two or more things are compared on the same points.

DescriptionList.description: Terms and their one-sentence definitions, or a record of key and value (G: groupId, A: artifactId). Only for terms the page uses; never a loose glossary.

DescriptionItem.description: One term and what it is, in a sentence (Markdown).

Accordion.description: Secondary detail that not everyone needs, folded away (special cases, troubleshooting, long reference). Nothing essential goes here: the page must make sense with every section closed.

AccordionItem.description: One folded section: its title and its content in Markdown.

Cards.description: A grid of cards for related things side by side: pages to go to, tools, or the references the page comes from (a book, a talk, a project), each a card with its link. Two columns, one on a phone.

Card.signature: Card(title: string, text?: string, href?: string, image?: string)
Card.description: One card: a title, an optional line, an optional link (the whole card opens it) and an optional image URL.

Logos.description: A row of technology or brand names with their logos, to name a stack without spending text (Java, Spring Boot, Vue, Docker...). Names only; the logos are looked up.

TerminalReplay.description: A terminal session played back: the commands typed, one after another, with their output. For a short sequence the reader will type and what it prints. A single command with no output is a CodeBlock instead.

TerminalEntry.signature: TerminalEntry(command: string, output?: string, comment?: string)
TerminalEntry.description: One command: what is typed, what it printed, and an optional comment saying what it is for.

AgentReplay.description: A session with an AI agent, played back step by step (what it is asked, what it reads and runs, what it answers), with a short note for each moment. The way to show how an agent works, rather than drawing it or describing it. One idea per session; say in the text that it is an example.

AgentPrompt.description: What the person asks the agent, with an optional note on what to notice.

AgentStep.signature: AgentStep(running: string, done: string, icon?: string, output?: string, note?: string, permission?: "ask-allow" | "ask-deny" | "deny")
AgentStep.description: Something the agent does on its way (search, read, run, edit): the line while it runs, the line once done, an optional icon, what it printed, a note, and whether it had to ask permission.

AgentAnswer.signature: AgentAnswer(text: string, code?: string, note?: string)
AgentAnswer.description: The agent's answer, with optional code it hands over and a note.

Chat.description: A short chat exchange, shown as a chat: to show what asking an assistant looks like. For an agent that acts, use AgentReplay.

ChatMessage.description: One message: who sends it (user or assistant) and its text in Markdown.

Figure.signature: Figure(label: string, parts: (Area | Chip | Label | Arrow | Group)[], layout?: "row" | "column" | "grid", caption?: string)
Figure.description: A drawing composed from tinted parts, for pieces that fit together or a flow: Areas, Chips, Labels and Arrows laid out in a row, a column or a grid, on a soft background. The label says in words what it shows. The way to draw most ideas; one colour per concept, the same in the whole page.

Group.description: Lays out parts in a row, a column or a grid inside a Figure, with no tint of its own: two Areas stacked at the end of a row, or four Areas in a grid. A row turns into a column on a phone.

Area.signature: Area(title: string, parts: (Chip | Label | Arrow)[], color?: "blue" | "violet" | "cyan" | "pink" | "yellow" | "grey" | "green" | "amber" | "red", icon?: string, note?: string, layout?: "row" | "column" | "grid")
Area.description: A larger tinted group with a title: a concept that holds others (Chips and Labels), as the harness round a model. Never an Area inside an Area.

Chip.signature: Chip(text: string, color?: "blue" | "violet" | "cyan" | "pink" | "yellow" | "grey" | "green" | "amber" | "red", icon?: string, note?: string)
Chip.description: A tinted part of a figure: a short name, an optional icon and an optional quieter note after it.

Label.description: A plain line in a figure, no tint: an icon and a short text, as one item of a list inside an Area. Its colour, if any, is for the text and icon (green/amber/red for yes/ask/no).

Arrow.description: A connector between the parts before and after it: an arrow that points along the layout (down on a phone), with an optional word on it ("calls").

Diagram.signature: Diagram(label: string, brief: string, caption?: string, svg?: string)
Diagram.description: A drawing the Figure pieces cannot make: a curve, a timeline, axes, a cycle, a shape that matters. Write a brief, not the drawing: a drawing model makes the SVG from it. Leave `svg` out.

Artifact.signature: Artifact(title: string, brief: string, height?: number, html?: string)
Artifact.description: A small interactive piece, only when touching it is the point (compare two behaviours live, a simulation, a calculator). At most one per page. Write a brief, not the code: a model writes the HTML from it. Leave `html` out.
